name: Havok

tenures.source: Wins the DWO World Tag Team Championship from The Merchants of Chaos in a Corona street fight at Holiday Bash (24 Dec 1996).

caption: Mr. Pink and Guy Stone, who won the DWO World Tag Team Championship from The Merchants of Chaos in a bloody Corona street fight at Holiday Bash.

identity.note: Namesake only; no shared operator, era or continuity with any of the other wings' individually-minted characters named Havok.

name: The Merchants of Chaos

tenures.source: Loses the DWO World Tag Team Championship to Havok in a Corona street fight at Holiday Bash (24 Dec 1996).

caption: The Psychotic Clerk and The Cashier, the DWO World Tag Team Champions dethroned by Havok in a Corona street fight at Holiday Bash.

name: The Lethal Alliance

tenures.source: An outside stable, described in-broadcast as having 'more members than an Exodus'; Dark Vanity and Razi Mahmood are its only two members named in the held record.

caption: An outside stable whose named membership in the surviving record is limited to Dark Vanity and Razi Mahmood, its interference deciding both of the year's World Title matches.

name: Sledge and Harris
caption: Teamed for the first time to win the DWO World Tag Team Championship in a ladder match at WrestleKade X, Sledge doing almost all of the work.

tenures.source: The Deadly Wrestling Organization's own WrestleKade X card, 31 October 2004.
tenures.note: Won the DWO World Tag Team Championship from The Riverhawks in a ladder match at WrestleKade X.

name: The Triad
caption: A stable named on WrestleKade X's own broadcast, its members backing each other up in separate matches on the same card; only J'ster and Joshua Barnes are named as members in the surviving text.

tenures.source: The Deadly Wrestling Organization's own WrestleKade X card, 31 October 2004.
tenures.note: J'ster is called the stable's own "Most Valuable Player" while interfering in the Five Pillars match; Joshua Barnes is separately called "J'ster's Triad partner" while interfering in the Main Event.
